# Test AUROC against a single-Gaussian baseline versus a 8-component GMM baseline
# figure: auroc_gmm_vs_single
# source: /home/paul/Code/Atoms_Carla/data/TFV6/results_alt/8 clusters/atoms_analysis_mode_2/results_per_perturbation.json + summary.json
# Generated by figure_notes.py — do not edit; regenerate with the figure.

    Each point is one detector family on one evaluation set. Above the diagonal = the GMM baseline scores higher.
    Circles are per-perturbation (that perturbation against the clean frames). The diamond is pooled AUROC over the whole mixed test set (1000 frames: 200 clean and 200 each of brightness / camera loss / Gaussian noise / PGD). Gaussian noise IS included.
    Because the split holds exactly 200 frames of each perturbation and all of them are scored against the same 200 clean frames, a pooled AUROC is identically the unweighted mean of the per-perturbation AUROCs in the pool. Verified to machine precision for every detector. The two are not competing quantities; only the set of perturbations in the pool distinguishes the figures. The diamond is therefore the centroid of the four circles of its own colour.
    'gain' below is GMM minus single, so a negative gain means clustering hurt that family.
